subject: koala
pitch: A sleepy koala hugging a eucalyptus branch. Soft ash-grey fur with a cream chest and cream-lined fluffy ears, a big black leathery nose, half-closed drowsy brown eyes, strong grey paws with dark claws, and a sprig of blue-green eucalyptus leaves in one hand, mid-munch.
reasoning:
I'm planning a single TypeScript module for a koala hugging a eucalyptus branch, sketching out the branch orientation and how the koala's body and arms should wrap around it to look natural.

Settling on the trunk positioned slightly in front with a stub branch extending backward for the koala's rump to sit on. I'm sketching the skeleton hierarchy—hips, chest, neck, head—building an upright pear-shaped body with a proportionally large head, then planning to construct the parts using simple geometric primitives like spheres and sweeps for the spine, with flattened spheres for the ears.

Defining joint hierarchy...

Adding a separate rump sphere for the hips, then switching to a paint function to handle coloring instead of relying on body sweep sectors -- using mottled grey for the base fur with a cream patch painted onto the chest and belly based on surface normal and position.

Now I'm building the head: a flattened sphere for the skull with low-poly shading, plus a small snout and a prominent black leathery nose placed on top of the muzzle.

Working out the facial details further—placing a rounded black nose, a cream-grey muzzle sphere, and drowsy half-closed eyes with small brown spheres partially covered by flattened grey eyelid shapes positioned slightly above and in front.

Placing the eye sphere so it pokes out slightly with a grey lid sphere covering the upper portion for a sleepy look. For the ears, I'm positioning large flattened spheres at the sides of the head angled outward-forward, with a smaller cream-colored inset sphere offset along that same direction for the inner ear detail.

Setting ring count to 10 with small outward-facing spikes for the fur texture. Now I'm adding a separate cream lower jaw sphere on the jaw bone, then positioning the koala's arms and shoulders to wrap around the trunk, with hands meeting at the front.

I need to adjust trunk depth and radius so it doesn't collide with the face or nose geometry—pushing the trunk further back to z=0.34 while keeping the arms long enough to reach around it, and placing one hand holding a sprig near the mouth.

Positioning the hand holding the eucalyptus sprig near the trunk, with the stem running up to the mouth so leaves poke out between the lips. I'm planning elongated blue-green leaf shapes extruded as outlines, plus extra leaf sprigs scattered higher on the trunk and a small side twig for visual variety.

Attaching the sprig to the hand joint, I'm placing shoulder, elbow, and wrist points for both arms so one hugs the trunk while the other holds the sprig near the front.

Still building hand geometry...

For the left sprig-holding hand I'll curl small finger capsules with claws toward the stem, while the other hand just hugs. Then I move to the legs, placing thighs, knees, and feet spread forward from the hips, wrapping around the stub that sits behind the trunk along -z.

Scattering small cone-shaped fur spikes across the body surface for texture, with grey tones on the body and cream near the chest, then placing a small jaw sphere on the jaw bone colored cream-grey.

Now setting up the mouth: posing the jaw bone open by a modest angle for a mid-munch look, aiming the jaw joint forward with sprigs poking from the mouth, and adding a dark interior shape to suggest the mouth cavity.

Now I'm defining the full color palette: fur tones, dark fur, cream, nose, brown, claw, bark tones, and leaf greens to use across the model.

Now I'm positioning the eucalyptus sprig itself: a thin stem rod running from the hand bone toward the mouth, with leaves attached at points along it, oriented outward away from the face.

Skipping ahead, I'm adding upper twigs branching off the trunk at a few heights with drooping leaf clusters at their tips, using a helper function to generate twig geometry and leaf placement.
